title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — Mock Exam #20

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — MOCK EXAM #20
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these is NOT alive? (1 mark)
   A. A plastic flower
   B. A grass blade
   C. A young mango tree
   D. A maize plant

2. Why should you not pull leaves off a young plant for fun? (1 mark)
   A. The leaves make the roots sweet
   B. The plant has too many leaves
   C. Leaves are heavy
   D. The plant needs its leaves to make food

3. What is the main job of leaves? (1 mark)
   A. Taking in water from the soil
   B. Making seeds
   C. Making food for the plant
   D. Holding the plant in the soil

4. In a seedling, what is the correct order of growth? (1 mark)
   A. Root, flower, seed
   B. Leaves, seed, root
   C. Seed, root, shoot with leaves
   D. Shoot, seed, root

5. Which of these is a root that we eat? (1 mark)
   A. Carrot
   B. Banana
   C. Maize grain
   D. Cabbage

6. Which of these is a mammal that lives in water? (1 mark)
   A. Crocodile
   B. Whale
   C. Frog
   D. Tilapia

7. A caterpillar changes into a butterfly. Which sign of life does this best show? (1 mark)
   A. Dying
   B. Breathing out
   C. Feeding only
   D. Growing

8. Which of these animals lays eggs? (1 mark)
   A. Cow
   B. Goat
   C. Hen
   D. Human

9. What is diarrhoea? (1 mark)
   A. A swollen stomach
   B. Passing loose watery faeces many times
   C. Passing hard dry faeces
   D. Food coming out of the mouth

10. Why should you chew your food well? (1 mark)
   A. It makes food heavier
   B. It stops you drinking water
   C. It makes food colder
   D. It makes food smaller for easier digestion

11. What is the solid waste passed out through the anus called? (1 mark)
   A. Faeces
   B. Saliva
   C. Blood
   D. Juice

12. Which state of matter is used in a cooking gas cylinder? (1 mark)
   A. Gas
   B. Solid
   C. Ice
   D. Powder

13. Sand pours like a liquid. What state is each grain? (1 mark)
   A. Gas
   B. Steam
   C. Liquid
   D. Solid

14. Why should waste bins have lids? (1 mark)
   A. To make waste rot faster
   B. To make them look nice
   C. To make waste heavier
   D. To keep out flies and rats

15. Which of these is non-decomposable? (1 mark)
   A. Dung
   B. Dry leaves
   C. Fruit peel
   D. Plastic bottle

16. Why is broken glass on the ground dangerous? (1 mark)
   A. It grows
   B. It can cut people and animals
   C. It rots
   D. It feeds the soil

17. Why are rotting waste heaps a health danger? (1 mark)
   A. They make soil red
   B. They attract flies and rats that spread diseases
   C. They make water sweet
   D. They cool the air

18. Which of these is a benefit of proper waste management? (1 mark)
   A. More flies
   B. More floods
   C. A clean and healthy environment
   D. More disease

19. A tap leaks 2 litres every hour. How much is wasted in 5 hours? (1 mark)
   A. 25 litres
   B. 10 litres
   C. 7 litres
   D. 2 litres

20. Why do we wash vegetables in a basin? (1 mark)
   A. It uses less water and the water can be reused
   B. It makes them cold
   C. It makes them heavier
   D. It wastes water

21. What is mulching? (1 mark)
   A. Burning grass
   B. Removing all plants
   C. Covering soil with dry grass or leaves
   D. Digging deep holes

22. Which of these uses less water to wash a car? (1 mark)
   A. A bucket and sponge
   B. A running hose
   C. A large drum poured everywhere
   D. A long shower

23. When is the best time to water plants? (1 mark)
   A. Early morning or evening
   B. Never
   C. Midday only
   D. Noon

24. When light hits an opaque object, what forms behind it? (1 mark)
   A. A shadow
   B. A rainbow
   C. A flame
   D. Sound

25. Which of these artificial sources charges its battery in the sun? (1 mark)
   A. Sun
   B. Lightning
   C. Stars
   D. Solar lamp

26. Which battery-powered device gives artificial light? (1 mark)
   A. Sun
   B. Stars
   C. Torch
   D. Firefly

27. Which of these should be kept away from fire? (1 mark)
   A. Salt
   B. Paraffin and petrol
   C. Clean water
   D. Stones

28. What should you do first if you burn your skin? (1 mark)
   A. Ignore it
   B. Put butter on it
   C. Cover it with soil
   D. Put it under cool running water and tell an adult

29. Which of these is a use of heat? (1 mark)
   A. Making light only
   B. Hearing sound
   C. Cooking food
   D. Making shadows

30. At what temperature does water boil? (1 mark)
   A. 0 degrees Celsius
   B. 50 degrees Celsius
   C. 10 degrees Celsius
   D. 100 degrees Celsius

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Give two examples each of transparent and opaque materials. (2 marks)

32. Explain the difference between diarrhoea and constipation. (4 marks)

33. Describe an activity to observe the growth of a bean seed. Include what you need, what you do and what you record. (5 marks)

34. Explain why a mirror or a shiny cup is not a source of light. (3 marks)

35. Compare solids, liquids and gases in terms of shape and volume. (4 marks)

36. Explain how a frog is similar to and different from a fish. (4 marks)

37. Name the two forces studied in this topic. (2 marks)

38. Describe how to show that metal passes heat more easily than wood. (3 marks)

39. Explain why a kilogram of stones and a kilogram of feathers have the same mass but not the same volume. (4 marks)

40. Why is chewing food well important? (2 marks)

41. Describe how you would make a dustbin from locally available materials. (4 marks)

42. Define matter and give two examples. (2 marks)

43. Why should you not touch a hot object to find out how hot it is? What should you use? (3 marks)

44. Suggest two ways to make toys or ornaments from waste and the materials needed. (4 marks)

45. Why do we use kitchen gloves when holding hot pots? (2 marks)

46. What happens in the large intestine? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — MOCK EXAM #20 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — A plastic flower
   A plastic flower is made by people and does not grow, respond or reproduce.

2. D — The plant needs its leaves to make food
   Leaves are the food factories of the plant.

3. C — Making food for the plant
   Leaves use sunlight, water and air to make food.

4. C — Seed, root, shoot with leaves
   The seed starts, a root comes out, then a shoot with leaves.

5. A — Carrot
   A carrot is a storage root. Cabbage is leaves, banana is a fruit and maize grain is a seed.

6. B — Whale
   A whale breathes air and feeds milk to its calf, so it is a mammal even though it lives in water.

7. D — Growing
   A caterpillar grows and changes form to become a butterfly.

8. C — Hen
   A hen lays eggs. The others give birth to live young.

9. B — Passing loose watery faeces many times
   Diarrhoea means loose watery faeces.

10. D — It makes food smaller for easier digestion
   Chewing breaks food into small pieces.

11. A — Faeces
   Faeces are the solid waste of the body.

12. A — Gas
   Cooking gas is a gas that burns to give heat.

13. D — Solid
   Each grain is a small solid.

14. D — To keep out flies and rats
   Covered bins reduce smell and pests.

15. D — Plastic bottle
   Plastic does not rot easily.

16. B — It can cut people and animals
   Sharp glass can injure.

17. B — They attract flies and rats that spread diseases
   Flies and rats carry germs.

18. C — A clean and healthy environment
   Proper waste management protects health and the environment.

19. B — 10 litres
   2 x 5 = 10 litres.

20. A — It uses less water and the water can be reused
   A basin limits water use and allows reuse.

21. C — Covering soil with dry grass or leaves
   Mulch reduces evaporation from the soil.

22. A — A bucket and sponge
   A bucket limits the water used.

23. A — Early morning or evening
   Less water evaporates when it is cooler.

24. A — A shadow
   Blocked light makes a shadow.

25. D — Solar lamp
   A solar lamp is made by people.

26. C — Torch
   A torch is made by people.

27. B — Paraffin and petrol
   Fuels can burn or explode.

28. D — Put it under cool running water and tell an adult
   Cool water reduces the burn.

29. C — Cooking food
   Heat cooks food.

30. D — 100 degrees Celsius
   Pure water boils at 100 degrees Celsius.

SECTION B
----
31. (2 marks)
   Answer: Transparent: clear glass, clear plastic, clean water. Opaque: wood, metal, stone.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each pair.

32. (4 marks)
   Answer: Diarrhoea is passing loose watery faeces many times and causes loss of water. Constipation is passing hard dry faeces with difficulty.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for each condition.

33. (5 marks)
   Answer: You need a tin or container, soil, a bean seed and water. Plant the seed, water a little each day, measure the shoot with a ruler every two days and record heights in a table. Observe roots and leaves.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for materials, 1 mark for planting, 1 mark for watering, 1 mark for measuring, 1 mark for recording.

34. (3 marks)
   Answer: It does not make its own light. It only reflects light that falls on it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for not making light, 1 mark for reflecting, 1 mark for explanation.

35. (4 marks)
   Answer: Solid: own shape and fixed volume. Liquid: takes shape of container, fixed volume. Gas: no shape and no fixed volume, fills the container.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each state with correct shape and volume, plus 1 mark for a comparison.

36. (4 marks)
   Answer: Both are vertebrates and have a backbone. A frog has moist skin and lives on land and in water, and a fish lives in water and has gills and fins.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for similarity and 2 marks for differences.

37. (2 marks)
   Answer: Gravity and friction.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: Put a metal spoon and a wooden spoon into a cup of warm water. After two minutes touch the top of each. The metal feels warmer so metal passes heat easily.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for set up, 1 mark for observation, 1 mark for conclusion.

39. (4 marks)
   Answer: Both have 1 kg of matter. The feathers take up more space than the stones so their volume is larger.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for equal mass, 1 mark for the meaning of mass, 1 mark for feathers taking more space, 1 mark for volume being space.

40. (2 marks)
   Answer: It breaks food into small pieces and makes digestion easier.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for small pieces and 1 mark for easier digestion.

41. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose a strong bucket, box or container. Cut and smooth the top and cover any sharp edge. Make a lid if possible. Paint a label saying waste only and put it in a suitable place.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: Matter is anything that has mass and takes up space. Examples: water, stone, air.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning and 1 mark for two examples.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: It can burn your skin. Use a thermometer.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for burns, 1 mark for using a thermometer, 1 mark for reason it is safe.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: A toy car from a box and bottle tops. Beads from rolled paper. A flower vase from a tin.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each toy and 1 mark for each list of materials.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: Gloves are poor passers of heat so they protect hands from burns.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for poor at passing heat and 1 mark for protection from burns.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: Water is taken back from the leftover food and the rest becomes faeces.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for water and 1 mark for faeces.
